race_context: Brownsburg Community School Corporation (BCSC) serves Brown and Lincoln townships in Hendricks County {bcsc_board} {bcsc_engage}. It reported 10,654 students in pre-K through grade 12 at the midpoint of the 2025-26 school year and 631 certified teachers; Kat Jessup is superintendent {bcsc_welcome}.

The five-member board serves four-year terms {bp_bcsc}. Seats: three Lincoln Township (Katie Dixon, president, term ending December 2026; Mike Wells; Matthew Freije), one Brown Township (Gordon Hayward, secretary) and one at-large (Jessica Heffernan, vice president, term ending December 2026) {bcsc_board}.

Two seats are on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot, one each, matching the state list's "vote for 1" {bcsc_board} {in_list}. At-large: Heffernan is not on the ballot, so the seat is open; three candidates are running {bcsc_board} {bp_bcsc}. Lincoln Township: incumbent Dixon faces Garen Carnes {bcsc_board} {bp_bcsc}. Aurora Verkamp is listed with the American Solidarity Party; the other four are listed as nonpartisan {in_list}.

Budget: BCSC says the 2023 law HB 1454 removed about $3.5 million a year from its Operations Fund and that SEA 1 (2025) removes more than $2 million a year more, requiring $7.9 million in cuts over three school years {bcsc_engage}. The district says it will start 2026-27 with 49 fewer staff and teacher positions, cutting $3.3 million, with more cuts expected in 2027-28 {bcsc_engage}.

Referendum: BCSC has no operating referendum and said it will not seek one in 2026, calling a referendum "an absolute last resort" {bcsc_engage}. It says it collects and spends less per student than similar districts while outperforming them on state metrics {bcsc_engage}.

Local support: the Town of Brownsburg approved a one-time $800,000 in TIF funds for BCSC workforce-development programs, and the Brown and Lincoln township trustees each pledged $100,000 toward transportation for homeless students under the McKinney-Vento program, which the district says costs over $300,000 a year {bcsc_engage}.
Community engagement: the district held three public finance sessions (Feb. 4, Feb. 25 and March 18, 2026) on school funding, SEA 1 and possible 2027-28 cuts {bcsc_engage}.

Forums: no candidate forum or news coverage of the 2026 race was found in reviewed sources. Ballotpedia surveys from Verkamp and Barker were the only detailed candidate statements found {bp_verkamp} {bp_barker}.

candidates.summary: Homeschooling parent and Hendricks County native running for the open at-large seat; listed with the American Solidarity Party {bp_verkamp} {in_list}.
background: Stay-at-home parent; graduated from the Indiana Academy for Science, Mathematics and Humanities and Indiana State University {bp_verkamp}.
A Hendricks County native who attended Pittsboro Elementary and Tri-West {bp_verkamp}.
Homeschools her children, who do not attend BCSC; she says a strong school system is a priority for every Brownsburg resident {bp_verkamp}.
path_to_ballot: Listed with the American Solidarity Party on the 2026 ballot list {in_list}.

items: Says teachers need flexibility to adapt lesson plans to the children in front of them rather than follow a rigid schedule, even one developed by district teachers {bp_verkamp}.
Says "Having the best test scores should not be the goal" and that schools should teach children how to learn {bp_verkamp}.
Wants significant outdoor time and physical movement, especially for elementary-age children {bp_verkamp}.
Says charter and magnet schools offer flexibility BCSC should use to enhance its offerings, while acknowledging this would require significant resources and time {bp_verkamp}.

on_incumbent: No comment on the current board's decisions was found.
plans: Says she looks forward to learning about BCSC from community members and through the Vision BCSC program {bp_verkamp}.

candidates.summary: Healthcare executive and BCSC parent running for the open at-large seat, listed as nonpartisan {bp_barker} {in_list}.
background: Has more than 20 years of leadership experience in healthcare organizations in strategy, operations and finance; bachelor's degree from Erskine College {bp_barker}.
Brownsburg resident since 2014 and parent of two BCSC students; in her fourth year on her elementary school's PSG board, now as president; graduate of the district's Vision BCSC program {bp_barker}.
path_to_ballot: Listed as nonpartisan on the 2026 ballot list {in_list}.

items: Says fiscal responsibility means understanding alternatives, seeking efficiencies, advocating for a sustainable funding structure and avoiding savings that create larger costs later {bp_barker}.
Says programs should be evaluated on outcomes, need, participation and cost, and the district should be willing to ask "what we can stop doing" {bp_barker}.
Says core classroom instruction should come first when resources are limited {bp_barker}.
Calls teacher retention critical, citing pay, workload, leadership, resources and professional growth {bp_barker}.
Wants a consistent process for major decisions: explain the issue and trade-offs early, take community input before deciding, then explain what was decided and why {bp_barker}.

on_incumbent: Says she wants "greater transparency and community understanding around significant decisions and changes," noting that current decisions are financial; no direct criticism of specific board votes was found {bp_barker}.
plans: Says she would help protect what makes Brownsburg schools strong while navigating financial challenges {bp_barker}.
